Scanner radio evaporates.

Said once, to whoever happened to be listening. Then gone.

NO REWIND · NO SEARCH · NO MEMORY

What this is

Police, fire, EMS, and transit radio across Greater Boston, transcribed as it is spoken. Every transmission is typed, located, threaded into incidents, archived with its own audio, and answerable in plain English.

Five verbs, and the rest is detail: it listens, it writes everything down, it figures out where, it threads calls into stories, and it checks its own work.

Built inside Boston Globe Media as a newsroom tool. Runs unattended.

Vercel serverless · Upstash Redis · Vercel Blob · models via OpenRouter · the only hardware we own is the radios

Verb one: it listens. Ten of these radios cover towns. The eleventh covers one building; hold that thought.

It writes everything down

THE RADIO SAID

“Coming in for an AMB in progress, 406 Meridian, apartment 11. Caller's stating the neighbor just assaulted her.”

fifteen seconds of air, gone unless somebody was listening · tuesday 8:58 a.m., east boston
THE ROW IT BECOMES
at         2026-08-18T12:58:06Z
feed       boston-police
callType   assault
units      AMB
address    406 Meridian St, Boston
lat, lon   42.38032, -71.03933
precision  exact
tier       2 (violence signal)
incident   inc-msyo4wyn · threaded
clip       ▶ audio, one tap from every claim

Sixteen thousand of these per two days. Each one is two API calls away from any question you can phrase.

It figures out where, and admits when it can’t

12,281
OF 16,075 FIXES IN 48H WERE WEAK: PLACEABLE ONLY AS “SOMEWHERE IN BOSTON”
EXACT 1,783 · APPROX 537 · WEAK 12,281

Three quarters of everything said on the air names no findable place. A weak fix is the town centroid, which for Boston is a spot by City Hall, and drawing them piled thousands of unrelated calls into a phantom mass incident at Government Center.

So a weak fix refuses to draw. The call keeps its card in every list; the map declines to state a place nobody said.

A wrong pin is worse than no pin.

It threads calls into stories

No transmission carries a story id. Stories are inferred: shared units, one place, one stretch of time.

It checks its own work

THE ANALYST
Reads batches of raw transcript and writes the situations board: headline, summary, location, priority. Good at narrative. Too eager, left alone.
→
THE JUDGE
Audits every claim against the transcript. A “confirmed” nobody said on air gets stripped. Severity with no root in the audio gets cut.
→
THE BOARD
What survives, printed with its scars: the screen literally says “model overruled” and why.

Quiet is an acceptable answer. “Could not make it out” is an acceptable answer. Guessing is not.

The two days’ hourly curves correlate at r = 0.86. Even the failure is recorded: the amber mark is our own relay outage, kept like everything else.

Medicals and alarms are the city’s background hum. Tier is the machine’s severity score: wounds, weapons, working fires, escalations.

The surfaces

THE MAP
Dots in call-type colors, situations ringed, venue calls squared. The wall of the operation.
THE BOARD + WIRE
Situations as an editor would brief them, over the raw transcript ticker as it happens.
LISTEN
The raw wall: any feed, live, several at once, straight off the air. Zero interpretation in the way.
THE ARCHIVE
Ask in English: “stabbing last night in Dorchester.” Time, type, place parsed; scenes returned with audio.
THE DESK
A running 20-minute read that is allowed to say “quiet.” Ask it questions; answers cite their clips.
SHIFT CHANGE
Sit down to the last 10 hours: what is open now, the major calls, the also-heard. A handoff, not a feed.

The wall, in a pocket

Native SwiftUI, six tabs: Map, Board, Listen, Archive, Shift, Desk. One shared radio player, chains transmissions oldest-first from any screen.

The phone holds no state the server does not own. Delete the app, reinstall it: the board is the board.

Audio keeps playing with the screen locked, which is how a night editor actually uses it.

Empty folder to running on a phone: one day.

What compounds

RECURRENCE
STATE ST · 73×Repeat places surface problem properties and corners. A year of this is a beat no official release provides.
THE PULSE
494 VS 140Peak vs. quietest hour, day-over-day r = 0.86. Baselines turn anomalies into pages: “tonight is 3× normal.”
RADIO GAP
BOS 7.4 · CAM 5.5 MINMedian dispatch voice to first field voice (n=112, n=25). By neighborhood, over a year, with audio receipts.
HOSPITAL FLOWS
BMC · 65 MENTIONSMore than the next three hospitals combined. Where the city’s ambulances actually go, heard nightly.
WORKLOAD
A1 · 372 TXOne ambulance dispatch voice, 372 transmissions in 48h. Staffing and fatigue curves fall out of this.
LEAD TIME
TO BE MEASUREDWhen the air first said it vs. when the statement landed. The head start, measured, over months.

~2.9M rows a year at today’s pace. A nightly file and a laptop. The move is to never stop recording.

What is hard, honestly

SPEECH
Scanner audio is brutal: codes, cross-talk, garble. It heard Storrow as “Zorro” in this deck’s own example.

Keep the clip one tap from every claim; a human ear settles it in seconds.
PLACE
Geocoders lie with confidence. “Boylston” is a two-mile street; hospital names are destinations, not scenes.

Grade every fix, refuse to draw the weak ones, let venues override geography.
MODELS
Language models write beautifully past their evidence. Left alone they confirm things nobody said.

A second model audits the first, and “quiet” is an acceptable answer.

The rule everywhere: the machine states less than it knows and shows its work.
